content: ATL/CTL/TSB model limitations: (1) Cold-start problem — new users have no history so CTL=0, TSB=0; ATL spikes on first session making readiness look terrible artificially. (2) The model treats all TSS equivalently (a rest-day 100 TSS == hard-day 100 TSS). (3) RPE-based load is serviceable (typically within 10-15% of power-based for trained athletes) but has more error on short high-intensity efforts. (4) Without normalization, users comparing their TSB to published TrainingPeaks ranges will be confused because constants differ. (5) Model needs at least 4-6 weeks of data before CTL stabilizes and readiness band becomes meaningful — users churning before that window will never see the product's value.
